transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, lately I've started catching myself thinking that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. And sometimes, on my drive home from school, I find myself wondering if my family and my students would be better off without me. It really scares me, honestly, because I don't want to actually do anything like that, but the thoughts are just... there.
Have you ever actually made a plan for how you might do this, or have you ever attempted to harm yourself?

No, I haven't made a plan or anything like that. And I've never tried to hurt myself. Like I said, it's more just... those thoughts popping into my head, like wondering if things would be easier if I just didn't wake up, or if people would be better off. But I don't actually want to do it, which is why it scares me so much.
Over the past few weeks or months, have you noticed a period where you felt persistently sad, empty, or down most of the day, nearly every day? If so, how long has that been going on?

Yes, I have. It's actually been going on for quite a while now, definitely longer than a few months. I'd say it's been about a year and seven months. It started right around the time I took over the STEM assessment redesign at my school, which was just piled on top of my regular teaching load. Ever since then, I've just felt that persistent sadness and emptiness pretty much every day.
Before this period that started about a year and seven months ago, have you ever experienced a similar stretch of time where you felt persistently sad, empty, or depressed for weeks or months?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days or stressful weeks before, like anyone else, but nothing like this. This feeling of just being down all the time... it really only started with that curriculum project. Before that, I felt pretty normal.

During this past year and seven months, or even before that, have you ever experienced a period lasting several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, euphoric, or 'on top of the world' — times when you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt rested and energized?

No, I haven't ever felt like that. I mean, there are times when I've been happy or excited about something, but never... unusually energetic or like I didn't need sleep. Honestly, I usually feel like I need more sleep, not less. So no, nothing like what you're describing.
During this past year and seven months when you've been feeling persistently sad and empty, how has your sleep been? Are you sleeping more than usual, less than usual, or about the same?

I'm definitely sleeping less than usual. I mean, I can be completely exhausted, but I'll just lie awake in bed replaying assessment deadlines and classroom mistakes in my head. And then, even when I do finally fall asleep, I usually end up waking up around 4 a.m. and... I never really get back to sleep after that.
During this past year and seven months, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight?

Yeah, there's definitely been a change. Most school days, I just forget to eat, or I end up avoiding it until late in the afternoon. I just don't have much of an appetite. And because of that, over the past year, my clothes have gotten noticeably looser. I'm really not trying to lose weight at all, it's just happening.
During this past year and seven months, have you noticed difficulty concentrating on tasks, making decisions, or do you find yourself feeling guilty or worthless?

Yes, concentrating has been really hard lately. I'll be grading assignments and I'll read the same student response three or four times and still not know what score to give it. Nothing seems to stick. And making decisions is just as bad. Even simple choices, like which lab supplies to order for the classroom, can stall me for an hour. I just can't seem to focus or make up my mind.

You mentioned having difficulty concentrating and making decisions. During this past year and seven months, have you been feeling guilty about things, or do you find yourself thinking that you're worthless or that you've failed in some way?

Yeah, I do. Um, I guess I feel like I'm failing a lot. Like, if a lesson goes badly at school, or even if just one student looks confused, I take it as proof that I'm letting everyone down. I just keep replaying it over and over in my head... and it makes me feel like I'm a terrible teacher, and honestly, a terrible mother, too.

You mentioned these symptoms started about a year and seven months ago when you took on the curriculum project. Just to be clear, did all of these symptoms — the sadness, the sleep problems, the appetite changes, the difficulty concentrating, and the feelings of guilt — all start around the same time, or did some of them develop gradually after that?

Yeah, they pretty much all started around the same time. Um, this has all been going on for about a year and seven months now. That was right when I took over the STEM assessment redesign, you know, on top of my regular teaching load. It just all seemed to start right then.

During this past year and seven months, have there been any stretches of time — say, 2 months or longer — where you felt noticeably better, where the sadness lifted or the symptoms eased up, even if just for a little while?

No, not really. Um, I don't think there's been any stretch like that. I mean, maybe I'll have a okay day here or there, but definitely not a whole two months where it lifted. It's just been pretty constant this whole time.

During this past year and seven months when you've been feeling so down, have you ever experienced anything unusual like hearing voices that others couldn't hear, or believing things that others told you weren't true — even if just for a brief moment?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've never heard voices or, you know, believed things that weren't true. It's just been the sadness and everything else we talked about.

During this past year and seven months, or even before that, have you ever noticed periods where your thoughts seemed to race, or where you felt like you were doing a lot of things at once — like you had a lot of projects or goals you were trying to accomplish all at the same time?

No, I don't think so. I mean, obviously I had a lot on my plate with the curriculum project and my regular classes, but it wasn't like my thoughts were racing or anything. I just felt overwhelmed by it all, not like I was trying to do a million things at once on purpose. So, no, nothing like that.
